newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges rethink by China on Hong Kong laws.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges rethink by China on Hong Kong laws.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was deeply concerned about attempts to water down civil liberties in Hong Kong and called on a China-controlled committee to reconsider a recommendation to amend laws there.

The so-called Preparatory Committee, meeting in Beijing on Sunday, listed 25 laws including the Bill of Rights and key electoral statutes that will either be axed or diluted when sovereignty over Hong Kong reverts to China on July 1.
"We are deeply concerned over any attempt to weaken civil liberties and basic freedoms in Hong Kong," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"We believe this recommendation should be re-examined, re-examined carefully against China's commitment to preserve human rights, freedom of the press and individual freedom in Hong Kong," Burns told a news briefing.
"Statements and recommendations of this kind do not help foster stability or confidence in Hong Kong," Burns said.

"We hope that China and the future Hong Kong government will consider seriously the damage that erosion of Hong Kong's civil liberties and basic freedoms could do to its way of life and its high degree of autonomy."
The United States would be raising the issue with the Beijing authorities before a final decision was taken on the matter, Burns said.

China's Xinhua news agency has said that in formulating the laws, the current British authorities in Hong Kong had violated a 1984 Sino-British treaty on the handover as well as the Basic Law, Hong Kong's post-handover constitution.
